whatItIs.text: A spongy nightshade berry — related to tomato and potato but from Eurasia — prized above all for absorbing oil and flavour like almost nothing else.

historyNote.text: Eggplant was probably domesticated twice from the wild thorn apple, once in South Asia and once in East Asia; the English name was first recorded in 1763 for white, hen's-egg-shaped varieties — China and India now grow 85% of the world's 61 million tonnes.

howToChoose.text: Choose heavy, glossy fruit with taut skin and a green cap that isn't dried; dull skin and light weight mean seeds have hardened and bitterness is coming.

storage.text: Keep at cool room temperature and use within days — eggplant dislikes fridge cold.

useItUp.text: Softening eggplant still roasts into baba ganoush or melts into curries and pasta sauces; salt it first to draw out bitterness and water.

substitutions.note: faster cooking, less spongy; grill or roast first
